text: The page gives two independent routes to 'heart failure likely'; only the orthopnoea-and-leg-swelling route is encoded. The second route (age ≥ 50 with a first episode of wheeze/tight chest) cannot be written because the grammar has no numeric age, but nothing in the file records that this branch was dropped, and a patient over 50 with first-episode wheeze and no leg swelling will get no heart failure prompt at all. ref: Emergency: life-threatening wheeze/tight chest; Urgent: severe wheeze/tight chest
text: Pulse is compared on 'Pulse, function' (8499008) and saturation on 'Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen' (103228002). SNOMED also has 'Heart rate' (364075005) and 'Peripheral oxygen saturation' (431314004), which are the usual observables for a pulse and a pulse-oximeter reading. Whether these clauses ever fire depends on which concept the vitals system records; I could not verify that from the permitted inputs. If the system records the other concept, pulse < 50, pulse > 120 and SpO2 < 90% are silently dead.

The page labels this branch 'Life threatening' and its management 'Refer urgently', the same words as the Severe branch; it never says 'emergency'. Emergency is a reasonable reading of the escalation above Severe but is a judgment the house standard asks to be explicit about.

'If first episode of wheeze/tight chest, assess for asthma and COPD' has no possible Asthma / COPD rule, although 'First episode' (qualifier value) and 'Asthma' (disorder) exist. Low consequence given the cross-reference to the asthma/COPD page.

The one-hour reassessment branch (talk normally, RR < 20 vs ≥ 20, PEFR improved by > 20%, worsening → manage as severe) is not modelled. This is a language limit (no treatment state, no change-over-time), and the worsening branch would not raise priority above the existing Urgent, so no triage outcome is lost; worth recording as could-not-model.

ref: Diagnose probable heart failure from wheeze/tight chest
text: The page gives two routes to 'heart failure likely': (difficulty breathing worse on lying flat AND leg swelling) OR (patient >= 50 years with first episode of wheeze/tight chest). The rule encodes only the first; the second is silently dropped, so an older patient with a first episode and no orthopnea/oedema never gets the probable diagnosis. The grammar has no patient-age comparison (only age groups), so the branch cannot be encoded exactly; it should at least be recorded as 'could not model', and an approximation considered (a probable or possible branch on the First-episode-qualified complaint, with the age left to the clinician). 'probable' for 'likely' and the and-structure of the first branch are right.

All six criteria and thresholds match 'Yes: Severe'. But the level is Urgent, identical to the base 'Urgent: wheeze/tight chest' rule, so this rule never changes the outcome. Either it is intentionally documentary, or the page's 'Refer urgently' for severe was meant to escalate above the mild/moderate case (which the page treats and reassesses for 3 hours before referring); the briefing reserves 'Very urgent' for explicit escalation, so this is a judgement call to record, not a defect.
